question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this gateway-local Teams identity and exact-resource authorization model as a permanent core and Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The branch crosses the recently established plugin-owned Workspaces boundary and permanently changes gateway identity, roles, protocol, storage, agent delegation, and public plugin APIs; repository behavior alone cannot authorize that product commitment.

options.title: Sponsor the complete Teams model
options.body: Accept the proposed first-party direction, then require the correctness fixes, security architecture review, migration proof, and real behavior evidence before merge.

options.title: Keep only generic primitives
options.body: Limit core to the minimum reusable identity and exact-resource authorization seams while retaining Teams invitations, sharing policy, approvals, and portal behavior in the Workspaces owner surface.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the gateway operator-oriented and close or defer the branch until a narrower sponsored product direction exists.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the complete Teams model
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed first-party direction, then require the correctness fixes, security architecture review, migration proof, and real behavior evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the Workspaces foundation and are best positioned to approve or preserve its current core/plugin ownership boundary.
